newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT - Hart cautions against changing Super 12.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT - Hart cautions against changing Super 12.

text.p: CHRISTCHURCH, March 21 - All Black rugby coach John Hart on Friday warned against any move to expand the successful Super 12 competition, NZPA reports.
Western Samoa has been pleading for a place in the competition which includes provincial sides from South African, Australian and New Zealand.

Victorian state coach Bruce Norton has said the All Blacks-Wallabies test at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on July 26 is the perfect opportunity to push for a fourth Australian team in an expanded Super 12 competition.
He said Perth or Melbourne based-sides would have equally good arguments to enter a team in a Super 16.
Australian chairman of selectors Michael Hawker has supported a Victorian team, boosted by interstate players, to be included in the competition.
Today Hart said there were dangers in changing the Super 12 system.

"My personal view is that the competition is hugely successful at present. Before you tinker with it, you need to give it two to three years in terms of reviewing its strengths and success," he told NZPA.
"I would be very concerned if the Super 12 season was extended without a total review of the integration of the international requirements of the three countries."
Hart said one of the merits of the Super 12 was that every year every side played every other side. If the competition was expanded and divided into two pools it would lose that appeal.

"It is important for the competition to be successful long term that it continues to be an even competition with a number of teams always contesting the top four spots and all teams having the ability to beat others."
On Western Samoa's tender for a place in the competition, Hart said a debate was needed at some stage on the whole issue of the island nation and its involvement in New Zealand rugby.
"At the moment I don't see how you can enter Western Samoa in a provincial competition. Western Samoa is a nation and that's an issue before you start.
"But I agree the game has got to be more global and we should be seeking to globalise the game. But you don't necessarily globalise it by one provincial competition."
The International Rugby Board should be looking at the competition structures which are emerging and have emerged as a result of professional rugby and money coming into the game.
"We should taking look at structuring what are the most appropriate competitions long term, which would help with the globalising the game.
"That may well be a provincial competition at provincial level which gets integrated by northern and southern hemisphere play-offs."
It might also mean a competition at international level which also leads to northern-southern hemisphere play-offs and may have a division one and two teams.
Meanwhile, Hart predicted the top rugby players could suffer burn out, because of the lengthening of the season from February to December, unless they were given more time to recover between seasons.
He said it would help it the All Blacks tour of England and Wales was reduced from the 13 games scheduled to seven or eight games.
The end-of-year tour itinerary for England (two tests) and Wales (one test) has not been completed.
New Zealand Rugby Football Union chief executive David Moffett was expected to resolve the end-of-season-tour issue in Hong Kong this weekend.
Hart will name two All Black trial teams after the Super 12 semifinals, and stage the trial week before the first test, against Fiji on June 14.
